paper.title: Multi-task Representation Learning with Stochastic Linear Bandits

unmapped: Multi-task: M_tasks linear contextual bandit tasks played in parallel for T rounds each; regret is summed over tasks
Task parameter matrix W = [w_1..w_T] (d x M_tasks) has rank r (shared low-dimensional linear representation); rank unknown to learner
Decision sets of K arms drawn i.i.d. from a zero-mean sub-Gaussian joint distribution on R^{Kd} (arms unbounded, x_k = Sigma_k^{1/2} z_k)
Arm distribution regularity (Assumption 2): skewness bound nu and omega_X condition; RSC condition on population covariance
Learner knows (an upper bound on) the noise variance sigma^2 and constants needed to set lambda_n (max ||Sigma_k||_op, C depending on c_eta, C_z)
settings.definition_quote: In this paper, we address the problem of simultaneously solving $T$ linear contextual bandit tasks. Each task $t\in[T]$ lasts for $N$ rounds and is associated with a regression vector $\w_t \in \reals^d$. ... The matrix $\W\in\reals^{d\times T}$ has rank $\rho(\W)=r$, with $r\ll \min(d,T)$. ... Our principal objective is to minimize the multi-task pseudo-regret $\Rbar(T,N) = \sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{n=1}^N (\x_{t,n}^* - \x_{t,n})^\top \w_t$

bound.regime: N >= N_0(delta) ~ C max_k||Sigma_k||^2 (r log d log(4TN/delta))^2

symbols.r_rank: rank of task matrix W (paper's r)

conditions: Assumptions 1-4: i.i.d. sub-Gaussian zero-mean arm distributions, arm distribution regularity (nu, omega_X), rank(W)=r, conditionally sub-Gaussian noise independent across tasks
Population multi-task covariance satisfies the RSC condition with kappa > 0

source.label: Th:MTLRegretBound
source.quote: Let Assumptions 1, 2, 3, 4 be satisfied. Assume that $\max_{t\in [T]}\norm{\w_t}_2{\leq}L$, for some constant $L>0$ and that $N\geq N_0(\delta)$ for some $\delta\in (0,1)$. Then, with probability at least $1-\delta$, the multi-task regret of Algorithm 1 is upper bounded (up to logarithmic factors) by $\bigO( (T\sqrt{rN}+\sqrt{rdTN}))$.

results.notes: Paper's N (rounds per task) mapped to canonical T; paper's T (tasks) declared M_tasks. Regret is the realized multi-task pseudo-regret (sum of mean gaps with per-round optimal arm) holding w.p. 1-delta. Constants depend on L, sigma, C_z, kappa, max||Sigma_k||. Lambda_n uses log N so horizon treated as known.
